utility.notes: ComEd is the dominant investor-owned electric utility for northern Illinois including the City of Chicago; this record's own permit terms explicitly reference ComEd electrical service connections.

value.name: Commonwealth Edison (ComEd)
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Chicago's residential solar customers this session (Illinois does have a municipal aggregation framework for default electricity supply, but that is separate from — and does not substitute for — the interconnection/net-metering relationship with the distribution utility, ComEd, which is recorded here).

permit_authority.value: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
permit_authority.notes: Illinois has no single statewide residential solar permitting rule — permitting authority sits with the local municipality (inside its corporate/home-rule boundaries) or the county (in unincorporated areas). Chicago's Department of Buildings is the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) for the City of Chicago specifically.

interconnection_url.notes: ComEd's own Residential Net Metering FAQ document (accessed this session) is dated 2023 (footer: 'NMR03-23'); Illinois's statewide 'Net Metering 2.0' policy reportedly ended full retail-rate net metering for newly-interconnecting residential systems after December 31, 2024 (per secondary reporting, not independently re-verified against ComEd's own current tariff this session). The mechanics described here (application process, credit rollover, SREC allocation via the Illinois Power Agency) are treated as still-current process facts; the specific credit VALUE/rate a new applicant receives today should be confirmed directly with ComEd before relying on it.

value.name: ComEd Distributed Generation (DG) Rebate — Energy Storage
value.description: ComEd's own Residential Net Metering FAQ states ComEd offers 'a similar rebate for energy storage' alongside its $300/kW solar Distributed Generation Rebate, without stating the exact storage-specific dollar figure on this particular document — see ComEd.com/DGRebate for current details, which was not independently fetched this session.
value.eligibility: Eligible energy storage systems paired with residential solar; exact eligibility criteria not independently confirmed this session.

battery_programs.notes: Recorded with status 'unknown' rather than 'active' because the exact battery-storage rebate rate was not stated on the document actually read this session — only that a rebate 'similar' to the solar rebate exists. See rebates for the solar-specific $300/kW figure, which was explicitly stated.

value.name: Structural design prepared and stamped by an Illinois-licensed architect or structural engineer

In-person existing-condition inspection report confirming (1) the structural capacity of the existing roof and (2) the condition of the existing electrical system, performed by the licensed architect/structural engineer or someone under their responsible control
Manufacturer's installation instructions for all primary electrical equipment (must be NRTL-listed and labeled)
value.required_when: always — must also be on site at the time of inspection

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own Express Permit Program (EPP) terms and conditions for Small-Scale Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Systems.

value: A pre-submission, in-person existing-condition inspection (structural + electrical) is required before the permit application is even filed
Post-installation, the system must be inspected by both the Chicago Department of Buildings and ComEd before it may be energized
A permanent rapid-shutdown label must be installed and verifiable at inspection if the system includes a rapid shutdown system, per the Chicago Fire Prevention Code
Any existing electrical deficiencies (including grounding/bonding) must be corrected by the licensed electrical contractor before solar equipment is connected

value.notes: Per the City's own page, qualifying Easy/Express Permit Program (EPP) projects (roof-mounted, output capacity under 13.44 kW) receive same-day permit approval — the City's own page states the permitting process for these projects 'was cut down from 30 days to one day.' Standard (non-EPP) plan review for larger/ground-mounted/non-qualifying systems is not itemized with a specific day-count on the pages read this session.

value.program_or_pathway: Express Permit Program (EPP) for roof-mounted systems under 13.44 kW output; standard plan review otherwise
other_conditions: EPP is roof-mounted only — it does not authorize wall-attached or ground-mounted solar PV components
EPP energy storage systems are capped at 20 kWh (10 kWh for non-lithium-ion batteries); only one installation is allowed per ComEd electrical service connection
Equipment may not be installed within 3 feet of a residential building's roof edge (4 feet for non-residential/mixed-use)

Electrical work must be performed by a Chicago-licensed electrical contractor; where required by Illinois law, work must be performed under a certified Illinois distributed generation installer (Illinois Commerce Commission) and roofing work under a valid Illinois roofing contractor license (IL Dept. of Financial and Professional Regulation)

value.name: Express Permit Program (EPP) solar PV permit fee
value.notes: Per the City's own page: the EPP fee schedule was reduced 25% from $375 to $275 for qualifying projects when the program was improved in 2013. This is the City's own currently-published figure, though the page's surrounding content references the original 2013 program launch and was not independently cross-checked against a separately-dated current fee schedule this session.

value.name: ComEd Distributed Generation (DG) Rebate — Solar
value.description: ComEd's own Residential Net Metering FAQ states ComEd offers a Distributed Generation (DG) Rebate of $300 per kW of installed capacity for eligible renewable generation systems.
value.eligibility: Eligible renewable (solar) generation systems interconnected with ComEd; exact eligibility criteria (caps, income limits, if any) not independently confirmed this session — see ComEd.com/DGRebate for current details.

rebates.notes: The $300/kW figure comes directly from ComEd's own official FAQ document, but that document is dated 2023 (footer: 'NMR03-23') and was not independently reconfirmed against ComEd's current, live DG Rebate page this session — status recorded as 'unknown' rather than 'active' for that reason, consistent with this dataset's standard of not marking an unconfirmed-current figure as verified-active. Separately, Illinois's Adjustable Block Program (SRECs, administered by the Illinois Power Agency) is a real, additional statewide incentive mechanism mentioned by ComEd's own FAQ, but no specific dollar/rate figure for it was independently verified this session and it is not recorded as a separate rebates entry.
